With the computation record and the holding-window excursions supported only as temporally co-occurring observations, no parameter value is justified from this phase.

Before any bounded numerical check is selected in a later phase, read the unread saved projected initial states for updates 0..34, the per-update backend deadline signals, and the remaining one-step prediction endpoints, so a probe does not rest on the 6-sample final window alone; a projected-model probe limited to an effective horizon of at most 0.01 s is known to be insufficient to explain an entire settling failure.

attribution.reason: reach_passed is true with terminal error 0.007642608585867386 m below the 0.01 m tolerance, while the final-window error maximum 0.05813810428573256 m exceeds the same 0.01 m limit and holding position is recorded as failed. The pass therefore describes the update-34 endpoint observation only, not the sampled holding-window behaviour; the retained summary also records the joint reach-and-holding criterion as false.

Holding position and holding speed are both recorded as failed (6-sample window error up to 0.05813810428573256 m versus a 0.01 m limit; speed 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s versus a 0.02 m/s limit). A terminal position pass with terminal speed 0.6351726092425104 m/s does not correspond to settled motion in this record.

The four reportable quantities are recorded under separate criteria with distinct coverage: terminal reach at one endpoint (update 34), holding position and holding speed over 6 samples of the final 0.05 s window, and computation over 35 retained updates with only selected per-update wall times. Nothing in the retained evidence promotes them beyond temporal co-occurrence, so they are reported as independently scoped observations.

No closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution capability exists in this context, and the timing record and holding window are recorded in different scopes (35 updates versus 6 window samples). Wall-clock overruns are synchronous and do not themselves establish skipped simulated updates, and a single execution does not establish a dominant cause; only temporal co-occurrence is supported.

A projected-model probe at an effective horizon of at most 0.01 s is not sufficient to explain an entire settling failure, and this phase performs no solve or evaluation (prediction_evaluations 0, local_solves 0). It is not the basis of any statement reported here.

facts.statement: Terminal reach criterion recorded as passed (reach_passed true) with terminal tip error 0.007642608585867386 m at the final retained update endpoint (t = 0.35 s) against a 0.01 m reach tolerance; terminal tip speed is recorded 0.6351726092425104 m/s. This is a single endpoint measurement of the last update, not a whole-trajectory range.

Sampled holding position recorded as failed (holding_position_passed false, sampled_settling_passed false). Over the 6 recorded samples of the final holding window (all recorded samples in the final 0.05 s window, t 0.3-0.35 s) the tip error count is 6 with minimum 0.007642608585867386 m and reported maximum late tip error 0.05813810428573256 m, straddling the 0.01 m settling position limit.

Sampled holding speed recorded as failed (holding_speed_passed false). Over the same 6 recorded samples the tip speed count is 6 with minimum 0.6351726092425104 m/s and maximum 1.5810152739742807 m/s against the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit; terminal tip speed is 0.6351726092425104 m/s, also above that limit.

Computation record: 35 retained controller updates at a recorded 0.01 s control period, with selected per-update wall times far exceeding one control period (update 27: 17.569447600049898 s; update 4: 17.893660200061277 s); stopping counts are 34 User_Requested_Stop versus 1 Solve_Succeeded, and full_snapshots_available is false.

limitations: Coverage as stated: terminal reach is one endpoint observation (final retained update, t = 0.35 s); holding position and holding speed each cover the 6 recorded samples of the final 0.05 s window (t 0.3-0.35 s); computation covers the 35 retained controller updates with only selected per-update wall times and no derived mean here. No whole-trajectory range is asserted.

The retained summary records joint_reach_holding_passed = false and deadline_misses = 35, but no matching handle for those two summary fields appears in the displayed context catalog, so they are reported as retained context rather than as handle-backed facts.

Retained limitations: no historical optimizer iterations or full warm plans are reconstructed, and a single execution and model comparisons do not establish a dominant cause. Full historical plans (control_snapshots.json) are not retained and full_snapshots_available is false.
Wall-clock misses and overruns are synchronous; they do not inject simulated delay or establish skipped simulated updates, and no simulated-delay claim is made here.

No closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution tool is available in this context (causal_identification is listed as unsupported), so any relationship between the computation record and the holding-window excursions is limited to temporal co-occurrence.

Only terminal_tip_speed_weight and holding_tip_speed_weight are eligible for future change under the explicit control grant; both are recorded at 0.0, and raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance without actual contributions or scaling.
